intro.line: Stage 1: The winding streets of Ghirapur.
A race across the Multiverse. Then, after the finish line, Tarkir's dragonstorms come back.

finale.line: With a swift motion Narset struck Sarkhan down. She would not let his fevered dreams of draconic dominance come to fruition. Not after all she had done to free Tarkir.
The storms calm. Sarkhan is free, and he is still dangerous.
Recorded: the race is over. The planes are still where they were.

villainFinale.line: With Taigam whispering encouragement in his ear, Sarkhan threw aside his misgivings. The ritual would return him to his former glory. All he needed was a dragon's heart.
In this version, Sarkhan feeds the storms until Tarkir is all dragons.

battles.title: Start Your Engines
battles.blurb: Chandra races through Ghirapur. The other drivers are not here to be friends.

scene.line: Racers! Start! Your! Engiiiiiines!
Loot is free to go where he wants, so let's make sure the kid gets there in one piece.
Start your engines: your speed starts at 1 and rises when opponents lose life. At max speed, your cards get their best effects.

villainScene.line: Caution is for those who falter.
Amonkhet champions become markedly more reckless after dying.

hero.half: Make them lose life to raise your speed.

battles.title: One-Shot Powers
battles.blurb: The Speed Demons race against Ketramose's team of Amonkhet champions.

scene.line: Good sportsmanship wins the crowd. Bad sportsmanship wins the race.
Many brought weapons to the race. This crew built theirs as they went.
Exhaust: an ability that can be used once and then is gone. Save it for the turn that matters.

villainScene.line: Let the past die so the future might live.
They too deserve to witness Amonkhet's rebirth.

hero.half: Use your exhaust ability on the key turn.

battles.title: The Mardu Charge
battles.blurb: Elspeth's warriors charge past Ketramose's pit crew.

scene.line: We follow the dragonstorms, and we take down any threats that emerge from them!
Mardu lightning rods disperse the energy of dragonstorms—or whatever happens to be touching the rods.
Mobilize: when the creature attacks, make tapped, attacking warrior tokens. A wide swing from one card.

villainScene.line: Wherever the racers go, help follows.
To keep up with the Grand Prix, reporters trained just as hard as the racers themselves.

hero.half: Attack with a mobilize creature for extra bodies.

battles.title: The Speed Demon
battles.blurb: The race's devil takes the wheel. The skyfarers have the speed to meet it in the air.

scene.line: Each step we take is a decision that changes the course of our futures. We must be careful where we tread.
This can't be right. I should cross-reference with the archives immediately.
Hold your counterspells for the Speed Demon itself. Let the smaller cars through.

villainScene.line: The doomed souls of the Speed Demons race in uneasy unity, each one hoping to escape their own fate.
Speedbrood racers are gregarious while not racing, but everyone must eat.

hero.half: Hold counters for the big car.

battles.title: Spells from the Grave
battles.blurb: Narset's school fights Sarkhan's clans across the dragonstorm plains.

deck.name: Narset's School
deck.label: tribute
deck.note: Jeskai is three colours; the white is dropped for our land pool.

scene.line: Beware dragonstorms that strike from the sea. Their size always disguises their force.
No one of us could have built all this alone. A clan, a school, hope for the future. Thank you all.
Harmonize: cast a spell from your graveyard by paying its harmonize cost. Your old spells are not gone.

villainScene.line: The best way to protect the citizens is to defend Arashin, not hunt dragonstorms across Tarkir.
So, these dragons intend to also manifest through a sandstorm? I take some offense to that.

hero.half: Recast a spell from the graveyard.

battles.title: Mono-Red vs Domain
battles.blurb: Spring 2025: mono-red aggro against a big green ramp deck.

deck.name: Domain Ramp
deck.label: tribute
deck.note: Domain Ramp is five colours; here the green ramp core is kept for our land pool.

scene.line: You wanted a fight. Now you've got two.
They feed on OIL? Where were they during the Phyrexian Invasion?!
Race them. Their big creatures arrive late. Burn them out first.

villainScene.line: The draconic power that flowed out from the dragonstorms imbued the landscape with draconic features—scales, claws, and appetites.
The power of the dragonstorms transformed not only the land but many of the creatures within it.

hero.half: Go face before the ramp deck lands anything.

battles.title: Izzet vs Dimir
battles.blurb: Spring 2025: Izzet prowess against a Dimir midrange deck.

scene.line: Excellent form, Jun! Just keep your weight on that back foot, and you'll master this in no time.
Elegance. Precision. Grace. Qualities that must be practiced in writing as well as combat.
Cast cheap spells to pump your creatures, and hit before their removal lines up.

villainScene.line: Their race ended much the same way it began, walking through a sandstorm on a world that ended long ago.
At the Tombs Before Time, the living of Amonkhet made vital alliances with the honored dead.

hero.half: Cast cheap spells to pump your creatures.

battles.title: Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant
battles.blurb: Sarkhan feeds the dragonstorms because he believes he is saving the dragons. The racers and the clans have to stop him.

scene.line: Elspeth saw their capture as an inconvenience, costing them precious time. Narset saw it as an opportunity to recruit allies to their cause.
The Abzan forces rallied to the call, driving back Sarkhan's feral dragon horde.
Kill his dragons the turn they land. He feeds the storm only as long as they live.

villainScene.line: Let the dragonstorms rage. Let what seeks sustenance feed. Let Tarkir be what it was always meant to be.
Rage. Greed. Arrogance. People only accuse dragons of what they fear in themselves.

hero.half: Kill his dragons the turn they land.

villain.win: Tarkir is what it was meant to be.

half.line: You are not saving them, Sarkhan. You are feeding on them.

battles.title: Izzet Prowess at Full Power
battles.blurb: Deep in the archive, a deck that wins with spells cast and creatures attacking.

archive.what: A blue-red deck of cheap creatures and cheap spells built around Cori-Steel Cutter.
archive.why: It was fast, hard to disrupt, and punished slow hands.
archive.beat: Kill the first two creatures. Keep your life above burn range.
archive.after: Later sets gave the format more removal and slowed it down.

deck.name: Izzet Prowess
deck.label: tribute
deck.note: Built from cards in this act's sets only. No single tournament list is copied.

scene.line: Jeskai scholars fashioned devices to forecast the behavior of the dragonstorms.
Kill the first two creatures and keep your life high.

villainScene.line: Dragonstorm chasers are not deterred by danger—they claim there is nothing like witnessing the land embracing the power of a storm.

after.line: Recorded: later sets gave the format more removal and slowed it down.
